about.title: Alhambra Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Alhambra is a city of about 85,000 in Los Angeles County, and a lot of its workforce moves along Valley Boulevard, Main Street, and Mission Road every day — delivery drivers, restaurant staff, construction crews, warehouse workers, and people who commute on the I-10. When one of them is hurt on the clock, the first question is usually about workers' compensation. In California, that system normally covers medical care and part of your lost wages no matter who was at fault, and it is typically the only claim you can bring against your employer. It is not the whole story, though. If a subcontractor, a property owner, a defective piece of equipment, or another driver contributed to what happened, a separate injury claim against that third party may be available. Those claims work differently and run on a two-year clock. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. We match Alhambra workers with independent attorneys who can look at both sides of the picture at no cost to you.

items.title: We Sort Out Comp vs. Third-Party Claims
items.desc: Workers' compensation is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent outside party can open a separate claim. The attorneys we connect you with know how to tell the two apart.

items.title: Deadlines Are Watched Closely
items.desc: California expects you to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days, and third-party claims carry a two-year deadline. Getting connected early means those dates don't slip by.

items.title: No Fee Unless There Is a Recovery
items.desc: Our service is free, and network attorneys take injury cases on contingency. If you are being pressured or punished at work for reporting an injury, that retaliation is illegal — and it is worth mentioning when you reach out.

items.question: I was rear-ended on the I-10 while making deliveries for my Alhambra employer. Is that only a workers' comp case?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Because you were working, workers' compensation would typically cover your medical care and part of your wages. But the driver who hit you is a third party, so you may also have a separate injury claim against that driver and their insurer. Alhambra recorded 301 injury collisions in 2025, many of them during the Friday afternoon commute, so this situation comes up more often than people expect.

items.question: I didn't tell my boss right away. Have I lost my rights?
items.answer: California asks you to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, so the sooner you do it, the better. Missing that window can complicate a comp claim, but it does not automatically end every option, and a third-party claim runs on its own two-year deadline. An attorney can look at your specific timeline before you assume the worst.
